info.name: Penpot Sync
info.summary: Your Penpot designs as native, organisable, backed-up Nextcloud files
info.description:
Penpot Sync turns a Nextcloud folder into a live mirror of a Penpot team.
Map a Penpot **team** to a folder and everything in it shows up: projects become folders, designs become real `.penpot` files with the Penpot icon. Click one and the live design opens in Penpot.
Nothing is matched on filename. Every file carries its design's id, so renaming, moving, copying, trashing and restoring never break the link — and re-running a sync never duplicates anything.
## ✨ What you can do
- 📁 **File your designs however you like** — the folder a design lands in becomes its Penpot project, at any depth - 🚚 **Move** a design between projects, or into another team — same design, same history - 🍝 **Copy** one, and get a real new design in Penpot - 🗑️ **Trash, restore and purge**, mirrored into Penpot's own trash - ➕ **Create** a design from the Files app, or drop a `.penpot` archive in to import it - 🖱️ **Open in Penpot** with a click - ⌨️ **Script all of it** — every admin action has an `occ` command
## 🗂️ The folder *is* the project
Penpot's hierarchy is rigid: team, then project, then design, with no sub-projects. Nextcloud is a file manager. So rather than force Penpot's flatness onto your folders, this teaches Penpot yours — a folder becomes a project the moment a design lands in it, and the path spells the name. A project called `Brand/2026` arrives here as two nested folders.
**Drafts is a state, not a folder.** A design that belongs to a team but no project simply sits at the root of the mapped folder. Filing it is a drag; un-filing it is a drag back.
## 🖌 It never edits a design Penpot already has
A `.penpot` export is an opaque archive of nested design data, so there is no "Edit as text" action and no content writeback. Design happens in Penpot; Nextcloud holds the archive and the click-through.
The one thing that travels upward is an archive Penpot has **never seen**: drop a `.penpot` into a mapped folder, or press **Sync to Penpot**, and it becomes a new design. Nothing existing is touched.
## 🗑️ Two trashes, and only one irreversible gesture
Penpot has a trash of its own, so trashing a design in Nextcloud is reversible on both sides — restore the file and the design comes back with its id, revision and history intact. Delete a design in Penpot and its mirror lands in your Nextcloud trash, never a hard delete.
Only emptying your Nextcloud trash destroys anything, and even then only a design still sitting in Penpot's trash.
## 🧭 Sync or Link — the folder decides
| Mode | The file holds | Keeps a copy? | |---|---|---| | **Link** *(default)* | A pointer — zero bytes | No — clicking it opens Penpot | | **Sync** | The real `.penpot` archive | Yes — yours to open offline |
The mode decides whether the bytes live on your Nextcloud, never whether the design can be opened. A `sync` mapping is therefore also a real backup: every design in the team, exported and versioned by Nextcloud.
## 🎨 Honest icons, honest dates
Designs register their own mimetype, so they wear the real Penpot icon instead of a generic archive glyph. And each file carries **the design's** created and modified dates rather than the sync's — so Recent, Popular files and sorting a folder by date all tell you the truth about your work.
📖 **[Full documentation, screenshots and the `occ` reference on GitHub](https://github.com/kubed-io/nextcloud-penpot#readme)**
Requires the `enable-access-tokens` flag on your Penpot instance — it is off by default upstream. This app is in early development: it works end to end and is covered by tests against a real Penpot, but has not yet been run widely.
